_about: ENHANCEMENT E16: the on-screen touch controls' look and layout, read by game/render/TouchControls (which has the same values built in, for when this file is missing or a field is). Replacing the art is a data-only change: put the new PNGs anywhere under game/data, point 'image' at them and adjust 'size' (what each is drawn at, stretched: an image needs at least that many pixels, in the same proportions) and the placement. Keep straight alpha and no exact magenta #FF00FF (the HUD keys it out). Units are logical pixels: the logical screen is always 768 tall, 1024 wide in the menus and in 4:3 levels, wider in widescreen levels, so sizes here are already relative to the screen's height. 'anchor' is the corner of the safe area a control hangs from and 'offset' the distance from that corner to its nearest edges, inward. 'hitPadding' is how far past its edge a finger still lands on it; 'shape' (circle or rect) is its touch area. 'scale' multiplies every size, offset and padding. Alphas are 0..1: 'idleAlpha' at rest, 'pressedAlpha' while held. A control with "enabled": false is not there at all (a layout without the combo buttons, say); one left out of this file keeps its built-in place and image. The first, placeholder look is images/touch/placeholder/touch_controls.json: copy it over this file to go back to it.
_provenance: The buttons are Magic Rampage's screen pad (Magic Rampage 7.8.7, Asantee Games; used with the authors' permission), made by tools/art/make_mr_touch_art.py from its package: images/touch/README.md says which image is which of its files and what was composed. Its buttons are 128 px squares (a 100 px face in a soft shadow), so they are touched as squares and drawn at 96-120. The layout is the port's own: the direction control under the left thumb; the actions under the right as a pad's face buttons, placed as E3 maps them (A jump at the bottom, X sword left, B fire right, Y light top); the two combo buttons in a row above them, each on its attack's side; pause and back in the top-right corner below the run's timer (setupScene.as:337 draws it at (W-50, 0)), clear of the player status frames at the top-left (interface.as). Keys starting with '_' are notes.

dpad._note: Left, right and down (K_LEFT, K_RIGHT, K_DOWN); no up, which only jumps. One round control the thumb slides on without lifting; 'deadZone' is the fraction of the radius at the centre that means nothing. Its look is Magic Rampage's buttons: the three arrows are each a whole button alone on a canvas the size of the control, where its direction's sector is (tools/art/make_mr_touch_art.py checks that every pixel of the left and right buttons is that direction alone), each brightened while its direction is held; the base image is empty (Magic Rampage has no disc). The knob, Magic Rampage's focus brackets, follows the thumb onto the button it holds; 'atRest' false draws nothing there while no thumb points a direction, since the brackets at the centre would frame the empty gap between the left and right buttons like a missing button (true keeps the knob at the centre, as the placeholder look's disc has it).

swordCombo._note: The sword combo as a macro of player 1's keys, one a tick: the way the wizard faces, again after a release, then K_S (CMD side, side, SWORD; playerInput.as:361). Waits first, if need be, for the combo buffer to empty (210 ms without a press, combo.as:116).

spellCombo._note: The spell combo as a macro: K_DOWN, the way the wizard faces, then K_D (CMD DOWN, side, SPELL; playerInput.as:380).

pause._note: K_ESC in a level or an arena: E13's pause. Magic Rampage's pause is a pill, 128x86.

back._note: K_ESC in the arena select, game over and the end screens: back to the menu (waitForInputToMenu, escToGoToMenu). Hidden in the main menu, in the options (the original's own Back arrow is there, clicked by a finger) and in the pause.
